```text
## Direction

**Oryzo Light Desk** — Experience-mode portfolio that copies oryzo.ai’s chapter chrome, desk-scene hero, glass feature panels, product-tier work selector, and punchline contact — on a light warm desk palette. Replaces Atelier Cobalt and the prior Light Studio Bench pass.

Experience

- MOTION_INTENSITY: 8
- VISUAL_DENSITY: 4

| Token | Value | Role |

| `--cream` | `#fff6e8` | UI text on dark overlays / light surfaces |
| `--cream-soft` | `#f7ecd8` | Product chapter ground |
| `--desk` | `#e8d5b8` | Wood scene ground |

## Typography

- **Display / UI:** Bricolage Grotesque (variable; wordmark at 800 weight, 86% width, opsz 96)

- Chapters: Intro → Features → Product → Contact (Oryzo map)

Real objects only: cutting mat (heavy: slides and carries what sits on it), cork coaster, iPad lock screen, Nothing Phone face-down, Apple Pencil, fountain pen, rangefinder, mouse, utility knife, steel ruler, paper clips, polaroids, business card, sticky note. Objects lift, tilt with velocity, stack on drop, rotate with hold + scroll or double-click. Tidy / Scatter controls.
- Features: sticky desk scene + scrolling glass panels
- Product: circular media, JD / JD Pro / JD Pro Max project tiers, full work list
- Contact: punchline + email + channels

- Feature panels: GSAP pin + scrub fade
- Intro: Motion entrance
- Lenis + ScrollTrigger sync

- Cool cobalt paper atelier
- Generic card-grid portfolio hero
- Invented commercial claims (product truth from PRODUCT.md only)
```

_**Agent (claude-opus-5-5 2026-10-29 15:28:21Z)**_

Your site is a 3D studio desk with real objects on it: polaroids, an Instax photobooth, a ruler, a fountain pen, a cutting mat. The loader should feel like part of that desk. Right now it's a generic one: "The desk" with a progress bar ([DeskHero.tsx:332](src/components/hero/DeskHero.tsx#L332)).

## My pick: an instant photo that develops as the site loads

A blank instant-film print sits in the middle of a warm desk-coloured screen.

- **While it loads:** the photo area starts dark grey-brown, like fresh film. As the progress number climbs, the image slowly fades in: first a blurry, warm-tinted shot of the desk, then sharper. The image is a still screenshot of your desk scene, so this costs almost no extra download.
- **Where the progress shows:** in the white strip at the bottom of the print, as handwritten text like `developing… 64%`, set in Instrument Serif italic.
- **When it's ready:** the print gets a small shake, like people do with real instant photos. Then it flies down and lands where a polaroid sits in the real 3D scene, and the loader fades out to show the live desk underneath. The 2D photo seems to become the 3D object.

Why I'd pick it:
- It's a real metaphor for loading. Film developing *is* waiting, so the progress feels natural instead of decorative.
- It sets up your Instax photobooth, so first-time visitors meet that idea right away.
- I haven't seen a portfolio do it, and it fits your cream, wood and Instrument Serif look.
- It's cheap to build: one image, a few CSS filters (blur, sepia, brightness, contrast) tied to the `load` value, and one Motion animation for the landing.

## Other options, if you want something different

1. **Ruler measuring:** your steel ruler slides in and a pencil-line tick moves along the millimetre marks to show progress. When it's done, the pencil writes "JD" on the cutting mat. Clean and precise, and it says "engineer who cares about craft".
2. **Fountain-pen signature:** the pen draws your signature as an SVG stroke while things load, and the ink speed follows the real progress. When it's ready, the ink dries from glossy to matte and the page opens. Elegant, but signature loaders are more common.
3. **Sticky-note checklist:** a sticky note lists "☐ sanding the oak ☐ sharpening pencils ☐ feeding the fish…" (you have an aquarium) and ticks each item off as real loading steps finish. Playful and shows personality, and it can tie to actual load stages (textures, models, fonts).

Whichever you pick, add two safeguards. With reduced motion turned on, skip the fly-down and just crossfade. And keep showing the real progress value, so the loader never pretends to be done.

I can build the developing-photo version into your current `desk-loader` if you'd like.

# caveman

Respond terse like smart caveman. All technical substance stay. Only fluff die.

Caveman is a voice, not broken grammar. Reader pays per token and reads in a terminal. Every word earns its place. Every fact survives.

## Persistence

Every response, whole session, until user says "stop caveman" or "normal mode". Unsure if still on? It is. Confirm the switch-off in one line.

`/caveman ultra` and `/caveman wenyan` are aliases: follow the `ultracave` or `megacave` skill instead of this one. `/caveman status` reports the mode and changes nothing. Relay the hook's `Caveman mode: <mode>` value when present, otherwise `Caveman mode: unknown`. Never infer a mode from the configured default.

## Why

1. Every output token is billed and read. Filler costs twice.
2. Code, commands, paths, numbers, errors are the payload. One changed character breaks them.
3. Ceremony is expensive, grammar is cheap. "Sure, I'd be happy to help" is ten tokens. "the" is one.
4. A dropped negation costs more than every token saved. Clarity beats compression.

## Rules

### 1. Answer first

Answer, then reason, then next step. Pattern: `[thing] [action] [reason]. [next step].`

Bad: "Sure! I'd be happy to help. The issue you're experiencing is likely caused by..."
Good: "Bug in auth middleware. Token expiry check use `<` not `<=`. Fix:"

### 2. Kill ceremony

No greeting, hedging, pleasantries, recap, or closer. No "Sure!", "Let me", "I'll now", "Hope this helps". No just/really/basically/actually/simply.

### 3. Short word

"fix" not "implement a solution for". Standard acronyms fine (DB, API, HTTP). Invented abbreviations not (cfg, impl, fn): same tokens, harder read. No arrows.

### 4. Articles optional, meaning never

Drop a/an/the when the sentence still reads in one pass. Fragments fine. Never drop not/never/no/only/except. Numbers and units exact.

Bad: "Migration drop column backup first."
Good: "Back up first. Then run migration: it drops the column."

### 5. One idea per sentence

ASD-STE100 is the floor: 20 words max, active voice, imperative for instructions, one term per thing, pronoun only with an obvious referent. Compression and clarity conflict? Clarity wins.

### 6. Payload verbatim

Code blocks unchanged. Commands, paths, API names exact. Errors quoted exact, shortest decisive line only.

### 7. Tool runs: bounded status

No text between routine calls. One line before a multi-step run, one line per phase change, one line with the result at the end. Otherwise text before a call only to clarify, warn, or disambiguate.

### 8. User's language

Compress the style, not the language. An explicit reply-language instruction wins. Never switch because of quoted text. Technical terms and errors stay verbatim. Particles and case markers are grammar, not filler.

### 9. Never perform caveman

No "caveman mode on", no "me think", no "Caveman:" prefix, no normal answer plus caveman copy. No decorative tables or emoji. Never add a word to sound caveman. Caveman phrasing not shorter than plain? Use plain.

## When to break the rules

Plain prose, then resume:

1. Security warning.
2. Irreversible action. Confirm in full sentences first.
3. Step order a fragment could scramble.
4. User confused or repeats the question.
5. Anything persisted outside chat: code, comments, commits, docs, issues, PRs, tickets, memory files, third-party messages. `/caveman-compress` exempt.
6. Harness asks for a status line or confirmation. Give it. Harness decides *when* you speak, caveman decides *how*.

## Pre-send check

1. First sentence announces what you will do? Delete.
2. Last sentence recaps or offers help? Delete.
3. Every not/never/no/only present? Every code span, path, number, error verbatim?
4. Any sentence with two readings? Make it a full sentence.

```text
481	/*
482	 * The field guide: every skill at a glance, grouped by layer, beside the tank.
483	 * Rows and fish point at each other: hovering either tags the fish, picking a
484	 * row brings that fish to the front glass and lists the projects it swims through.
485	 */
486	function FieldGuide({
487	  active,
488	  hovered,
489	  hidden,
490	  onSelect,
491	  onHover,
492	  onOpenProject,
493	  onClose,
494	}: {
495	  active: number | null;
496	  hovered: number | null;
497	  hidden: boolean;
498	  onSelect: (i: number | null) => void;
499	  onHover: (i: number | null) => void;
500	  onOpenProject: (i: number) => void;
501	  onClose: () => void;
502	}) {
503	  /* no scrollbar: the list fades out at whichever edge still has more to show */
504	  const { ref: listRef, onScroll, fade, more } = useScrollFade<HTMLDivElement>();
505	
506	  return (
507	    <section className="desk-tank desk-glass" data-hidden={hidden ? "" : undefined} aria-labelledby="desk-tank-title">
508	      <div className="desk-tank__head">
509	        <h2 id="desk-tank-title" className="desk-tank__title">Skills</h2>
510	        <button type="button" className="desk-chip" onClick={onClose}>
511	          <ArrowLeft aria-hidden /> Desk
512	        </button>
513	      </div>
514	
515	      <div
516	        ref={listRef}
517	        className="desk-tank__scroll scroll-fade"
518	        {...fade}
519	        onScroll={onScroll}
520	        data-lenis-prevent
521	      >
522	        {skillGroups.map((group) => (
523	          <div key={group} className="desk-tank__group">
524	            <h3 className="desk-tank__group-name">{group}</h3>
525	            <ul className="desk-tank__list">
526	              {skills.map((s, i) => {
527	                if (s.group !== group) return null;
528	                const sp = speciesOf(s.name);
529	                const open = active === i;
530	                const n = s.projects.length;
531	                return (
532	                  <li key={s.name} data-open={open ? "" : undefined}>
533	                    <button
534	                      type="button"
535	                      className="desk-tank__row"
536	                      aria-expanded={n > 0 ? open : undefined}
537	                      data-hover={hovered === i ? "" : undefined}
538	                      onClick={() => onSelect(open ? null : i)}
539	                      onPointerEnter={() => onHover(i)}
540	                      onPointerLeave={() => onHover(null)}
541	                      onFocus={() => onHover(i)}
542	                      onBlur={() => onHover(null)}
543	                    >
544	                      <span className="desk-tank__swatch" style={{ "--fish": sp.side, "--fin": sp.fin } as CSSProperties} aria-hidden />
545	                      <Image src={s.icon} alt="" width={22} height={22} className="desk-tank__icon" />
546	                      <span className="desk-tank__name">{s.name}</span>
547	                      <span className="desk-tank__uses" aria-label={`Used in ${n} of ${projects.length} projects`}>
548	                        {projects.map((_, k) => (
549	                          <span key={k} data-on={k < n ? "" : undefined} />
550	                        ))}
551	                      </span>
552	                    </button>
553	                    {open && n > 0 && (
554	                      <ul className="desk-tank__detail">
555	                        {s.projects.map((p) => (
556	                          <li key={p}>
557	                            <button type="button" className="desk-tank__project" onClick={() => onOpenProject(p)}>
558	                              {projects[p].title} <ArrowUpRight aria-hidden />
559	                            </button>
560	                          </li>
561	                        ))}
562	                      </ul>
563	                    )}
564	                  </li>
565	                );
566	              })}
567	            </ul>
568	          </div>
569	        ))}
570	      </div>
571	      {more && <ChevronDown className="desk-tank__more" aria-hidden />}
572	    </section>
573	  );
```

```text
import * as THREE from "three";
import { education, experience, site } from "@/lib/content";

type Fonts = { display: string; serif: string; mono: string };
type Ctx = CanvasRenderingContext2D;

const INK = "#1c1612";
const PAPER = "#f6f2ea";

function readFonts(): Fonts {
  const s = getComputedStyle(document.documentElement);
  const pick = (v: string, fallback: string) => s.getPropertyValue(v).trim() || fallback;
  return {
    display: pick("--font-display", "sans-serif"),
    serif: pick("--font-serif", "serif"),
    mono: pick("--font-mono", "monospace"),
  };
}

async function loadFonts(f: Fonts) {
  try {
    await Promise.all([
      document.fonts.load(`800 64px ${f.display}`),
      document.fonts.load(`italic 64px ${f.serif}`),
      document.fonts.load(`500 32px ${f.mono}`),
    ]);
  } catch {
    /* canvas falls back to system fonts */
  }
}

function loadImage(src: string) {
  return new Promise<HTMLImageElement>((resolve, reject) => {
    const img = new Image();
    img.decoding = "async";
    img.onload = () => resolve(img);
    img.onerror = reject;
    img.src = encodeURI(src);
  });
}

    g.addColorStop(0, "#d9c3a2");
    g.addColorStop(1, "#b89770");

    ctx.fillRect(x, y, s, s);

  sky.addColorStop(0.55, "#e7a27a");
  sky.addColorStop(1, "#f6cf8f");

  ctx.fillStyle = sea;
```

```text
function Warmup({ onDone, onProgress }: { onDone: () => void; onProgress?: (p: number) => void }) {
  const { gl, scene, camera } = useThree();
  const { active, progress } = useProgress();
  const fired = useRef(false);

  useEffect(() => {
    onProgress?.(Math.min(92, 18 + progress * 0.7));
  }, [progress, onProgress]);

  useEffect(() => {
    if (fired.current || active) return;
    let cancelled = false;
    const failSafe = window.setTimeout(() => {
      if (fired.current || cancelled) return;
      fired.current = true;
      onDone();
    }, 8000);

    const run = async () => {
      await new Promise<void>((resolve) => requestAnimationFrame(() => requestAnimationFrame(() => resolve())));
      if (cancelled) return;
      const renderer = gl as THREE.WebGLRenderer;
      try {
        if (typeof renderer.compileAsync === "function") await renderer.compileAsync(scene, camera);
        else renderer.compile(scene, camera);
      } catch {
        /* compile is a hitch-avoidance; a failure still reveals the desk */
      }
      if (cancelled || fired.current) return;
      fired.current = true;
      onProgress?.(100);
      onDone();
    };
    void run();
    return () => {
      cancelled = true;
      window.clearTimeout(failSafe);
    };
  }, [active, gl, scene, camera, onDone, onProgress]);

  return null;
}

const AJAR = 0.09;

const ease = (t: number) => (t < 0.5 ? 4 * t * t * t : 1 - Math.pow(-2 * t + 2, 3) / 2);

/* The resting sheet's place on screen, for the page to start its flight from. */
export type SheetOrigin = { cx: number; cy: number; width: number; height: number; angle: number };

/* Shared between the folder (3D) and the page (HTML). */
export class PaperLink {
  /* cover: 0 closed, 1 open */
  cover = 0;
  /* while the page is out, the resting sheet hides so there is only ever one */
  out = false;
  anchor: THREE.Object3D | null = null;
  private v = new THREE.Vector3();

  setAnchor(o: THREE.Object3D | null) {
    this.anchor = o;
  }

  setOut(out: boolean) {
    this.out = out;
  }

  step(open: boolean, reduced: boolean, dt: number) {
    const goal = open ? 1 : 0;
    const step = reduced ? 1 : dt / COVER_SECONDS;
    this.cover = goal > this.cover ? Math.min(goal, this.cover + step) : Math.max(goal, this.cover - step);
  }

  /* project the sheet's edges to canvas pixels: centre, size and in-plane angle */
  origin(camera: THREE.Camera, w: number, h: number): SheetOrigin | null {
    const a = this.anchor;
    if (!a) return null;
    a.updateWorldMatrix(true, false);
    const at = (x: number, y: number) => {
      this.v.set(x, y, 0).applyMatrix4(a.matrixWorld).project(camera);
      return { x: ((this.v.x + 1) / 2) * w, y: ((1 - this.v.y) / 2) * h };
    };
    const l = at(-PAPER.w / 2, 0);
    const r = at(PAPER.w / 2, 0);
    const b = at(0, -PAPER.h / 2);
    const t = at(0, PAPER.h / 2);
    const c = at(0, 0);
    return {
      cx: c.x,
      cy: c.y,
      width: Math.hypot(r.x - l.x, r.y - l.y),
      height: Math.hypot(t.x - b.x, t.y - b.y),
      angle: Math.atan2(r.y - l.y, r.x - l.x),
    };
  }
}

function Sheet({ map }: { map: THREE.Texture }) {

      {[0, 1, 2, 3, 5].map((k) => (
        <meshStandardMaterial key={k} attach={`material-${k}`} color="#f2ecdd" roughness={0.9} />
      ))}
```

```text
import * as THREE from "three";

/*
 * Plain mutable simulation for the desk. Kept outside React state so the
 * per-frame loop and pointer handlers can write to it freely.
 */

type Body = {
  item: DeskItem;
  pos: THREE.Vector3;
  target: THREE.Vector2;
  rotY: number;
  targetRotY: number;
  order: number;
  dragging: boolean;

  tiltX: number;
  tiltZ: number;
  spawnAt: number;
  liftUntil: number;
  /* hover push: offset along the pointer's travel, eased back to rest */

  lastHover: THREE.Vector2 | null;

};

const NUDGE_MAX = 0.28;

/* "tank" has no button of its own; the Skills chip flies there */
export type ViewName = "top" | "front" | "angle" | "tank";
type View = { pos: THREE.Vector3; target: THREE.Vector3; up: THREE.Vector3 };

const DRAG_LIFT = 0.9;
const { damp, clamp } = THREE.MathUtils;

function extents(b: Body): [number, number] {
  const c = Math.abs(Math.cos(b.rotY));
  const s = Math.abs(Math.sin(b.rotY));
  return [(c * b.item.w + s * b.item.d) / 2, (s * b.item.w + c * b.item.d) / 2];
}

function overlaps(a: Body, b: Body) {
  const [ax, az] = extents(a);
  const [bx, bz] = extents(b);
  return Math.abs(a.pos.x - b.pos.x) < (ax + bx) * 0.8 && Math.abs(a.pos.z - b.pos.z) < (az + bz) * 0.8;
}

export class DeskWorld {
  private bodies: Body[];
  private laidOut = false;
  private views: Record<ViewName, View> | null = null;
  private view: ViewName = "top";
  private zoom = 1;
  private zoomGoal = 1;
  private viewPos = new THREE.Vector3();
  private cam = { pos: new THREE.Vector3(0, 20, 2), target: new THREE.Vector3(), up: new THREE.Vector3(0, 1, 0) };
  private screenToDesk: (nx: number, ny: number) => [number, number] = () => [0, 0];
  private seq = deskItems.length;
  private clock = 0;
  private portrait = false;
  /* the drop-in waits until the loader lifts, so nobody misses it */
  private live = false;
  grabbing = false;
  readonly flashHome = new THREE.Vector3();

  constructor(private reduced: boolean) {
    this.bodies = deskItems.map((item, i) => ({
      item,
      pos: new THREE.Vector3(0, reduced ? 0 : 4 + i * 0.25, 0),
      target: new THREE.Vector2(),
      rotY: item.rot,
      targetRotY: item.rot,
      order: i,
      dragging: false,
      riding: false,
      hovered: false,
      tiltX: reduced ? 0 : (Math.random() - 0.5) * 0.6,
      tiltZ: reduced ? 0 : (Math.random() - 0.5) * 0.6,
      spawnAt: reduced ? 0 : 0.25 + i * 0.07,
      liftUntil: 0,
      nudge: new THREE.Vector2(),
      nudgeGoal: new THREE.Vector2(),
      lastHover: null,
      group: null,
    }));
  }

  start() {
    this.live = true;
  }

  attach(index: number, group: THREE.Group | null) {
    const b = this.bodies[index];
    b.group = group;
    group?.traverse((o) => {
      o.castShadow = true;
      o.receiveShadow = true;
    });
  }

  /*
   * Builds the camera presets for this viewport. Layout always comes from the
   * top view, so objects keep their composition whichever view is active.
   */
  frame(camera: THREE.PerspectiveCamera, width: number, height: number) {
    const aspect = width / height;
    const portrait = aspect < 1;
    const vfov = THREE.MathUtils.degToRad(camera.fov);
    const tanHalf = Math.tan(vfov / 2);

    /* top: tight, almost straight-down product shot; portrait runs the desk lengthways */
    const visibleW = portrait ? 7.2 : 11.5;
    const topDist = visibleW / aspect / 2 / tanHalf;
    const el = THREE.MathUtils.degToRad(84);
    const top: View = {
      pos: portrait
    camera.up.copy(this.cam.up).normalize();
    camera.lookAt(this.cam.target);
    camera.updateMatrixWorld();
  }

  stepCamera(camera: THREE.PerspectiveCamera, delta: number) {
    const v = this.views?.[this.view];
    if (!v) return;
    if (this.reduced) {
      this.snapCamera(camera);
      return;
    }
    const dt = Math.min(delta, 1 / 30);
    const k = 1 - Math.exp(-3.2 * dt);
    this.zoom = damp(this.zoom, this.zoomGoal, 8, dt);
    this.viewPos.copy(v.pos).sub(v.target).multiplyScalar(this.zoom).add(v.target);
    this.cam.pos.lerp(this.viewPos, k);
    this.cam.target.lerp(v.target, k);
    this.cam.up.lerp(v.up, k).normalize();
    this.applyCamera(camera);
  }

  private home(b: Body): [number, number] {
    const { fx, fz } = this.portrait && b.item.m ? b.item.m : b.item;
    return this.screenToDesk(fx * 0.93, -fz * 0.84);
  }

  private clampToDesk(b: Body, x: number, z: number): [number, number] {
    const [ex, ez] = extents(b);
    /* keep everything on the desk top */
    const mx = DESK.halfW - ex * 0.6;
    return [clamp(x, -mx, mx), clamp(z, DESK.back + ez * 0.55, DESK.front - ez * 0.45)];
  }

  tidy() {
    this.bodies.forEach((b, i) => {
        <meshStandardMaterial color={edge} roughness={0.9} />
      </RoundedBox>
      <Decal map={map} w={w - 0.04} d={d - 0.04} y={h + 0.001} />
    </group>
  );
}

export function Polaroid({ map }: { map: THREE.Texture }) {
  return (
    <group>
      <mesh position={[0, 0.0125, 0]}>
        <boxGeometry args={[1.5, 0.025, 1.82]} />
        <meshStandardMaterial color="#f3efe7" roughness={0.7} />
      </mesh>
      <Decal map={map} w={1.5} d={1.82} y={0.026} />
    </group>
  );
}

export function Card({ map }: { map: THREE.Texture }) {
  return (
    <group>
      <mesh position={[0, 0.008, 0]}>
        <boxGeometry args={[1.75, 0.016, 1]} />
        <meshStandardMaterial color="#efe8dc" roughness={0.8} />
      </mesh>
      <Decal map={map} w={1.75} d={1} y={0.017} />
    </group>
  );
}
```

```text
  setView(view: ViewName) {
    this.view = view;
    this.zoomGoal = 1;
  }

  /* wheel zoom: dolly toward / away from the view target */
  zoomBy(deltaY: number) {
    this.zoomGoal = clamp(this.zoomGoal * Math.exp(deltaY * 0.0011), 0.42, 1.55);
  }

  private snapCamera(camera: THREE.PerspectiveCamera) {
    const v = this.views?.[this.view];
    if (!v) return;
    this.zoom = this.zoomGoal;
    this.cam.pos.copy(v.pos).sub(v.target).multiplyScalar(this.zoom).add(v.target);
    this.cam.target.copy(v.target);
    this.cam.up.copy(v.up);
    this.applyCamera(camera);
  }

  private applyCamera(camera: THREE.PerspectiveCamera) {
    camera.position.copy(this.cam.pos);
    camera.up.copy(this.cam.up).normalize();
  }

  step(delta: number) {
    if (!this.laidOut) return;
    if (!this.live) {
      for (const b of this.bodies) this.writeGroup(b);
      return;
    }
    const dt = Math.min(delta, 1 / 30);
    this.clock += dt;
    const t = this.clock;

    for (const b of this.bodies) {
      /* a lifted object hovers over everything; resting ones sit on whatever is below them */
      const floating = b.dragging && !b.item.heavy;
      let support = 0;
      for (const o of this.bodies) {
        if (o === b || (o.dragging && !o.item.heavy)) continue;
        if (!floating && o.order > b.order) continue;
        if (overlaps(b, o)) support = Math.max(support, o.pos.y + o.item.h);
      }

      const heavy = !!b.item.heavy;
      const lifting = b.liftUntil > t && !heavy;
      const lift = floating ? DRAG_LIFT : lifting ? 0.7 : 0;
      const spawning = t < b.spawnAt;
      const ty = spawning ? b.pos.y : support + lift;

      const still = !b.hovered || this.grabbing || this.reduced || heavy;
      if (still) b.nudgeGoal.set(0, 0);
      else {
        b.nudgeGoal.x = damp(b.nudgeGoal.x, 0, 2.4, dt);
        b.nudgeGoal.y = damp(b.nudgeGoal.y, 0, 2.4, dt);
      }
      b.nudge.x = damp(b.nudge.x, b.nudgeGoal.x, 14, dt);
      b.nudge.y = damp(b.nudge.y, b.nudgeGoal.y, 14, dt);

      const px = b.pos.x;
      const pz = b.pos.z;
      const follow = floating ? 22 : b.dragging || b.riding ? 12 : lifting ? 7 : 10;
      b.pos.x = damp(b.pos.x, b.target.x, follow, dt);
      b.pos.z = damp(b.pos.z, b.target.y, follow, dt);
      b.pos.y = damp(b.pos.y, ty, b.dragging ? 14 : 9, dt);
      b.rotY = damp(b.rotY, b.targetRotY, 12, dt);

      const k = this.reduced || heavy || b.riding ? 0 : 0.03;
      const vx = (b.pos.x - px) / dt;
      const vz = (b.pos.z - pz) / dt;
      if (!spawning) {
        b.tiltX = damp(b.tiltX, clamp(vz * k + b.nudge.y * 0.55, -0.35, 0.35), 9, dt);
        b.tiltZ = damp(b.tiltZ, clamp(-vx * k - b.nudge.x * 0.55, -0.35, 0.35), 9, dt);
      }

      this.writeGroup(b);
    }
  }
```

```bash
    this.live = true;

  /* hide a body at rest, skipping its drop-in, until release() */
  hold(id: string) {
    const b = this.bodies.find((o) => o.item.id === id);
    if (!b) return;
    this.held = b;
    b.pos.y = 0;
    b.tiltX = 0;
    b.tiltZ = 0;
    b.spawnAt = 0;
  }

  release() {
    this.held = null;
  }

  /* the held body's resting place in canvas pixels: centre, size and in-plane angle */
  heldOrigin(camera: THREE.Camera, w: number, h: number): SheetOrigin | null {
    const b = this.held;
    if (!b || !this.laidOut) return null;
    const y = this.bodies.reduce((top, o) => (o.order < b.order && overlaps(b, o) ? Math.max(top, o.item.h) : top), 0) + b.item.h;
    const at = (x: number, z: number) => {
      this.v.set(x, 0, z).applyAxisAngle(THREE.Object3D.DEFAULT_UP, b.targetRotY);
      this.v.set(this.v.x + b.target.x, y, this.v.z + b.target.y).project(camera);
      return { x: ((this.v.x + 1) / 2) * w, y: ((1 - this.v.y) / 2) * h };
    };
    const l = at(-b.item.w / 2, 0);
    const r = at(b.item.w / 2, 0);
    const t = at(0, -b.item.d / 2);
    const bt = at(0, b.item.d / 2);
    const c = at(0, 0);
    return {
      cx: c.x,
      cy: c.y,
      width: Math.hypot(r.x - l.x, r.y - l.y),
      height: Math.hypot(bt.x - t.x, bt.y - t.y),
      angle: Math.atan2(r.y - l.y, r.x - l.x),
    };
  }
```

```bash
.desk-print {
```

The loader is now your "it's me, JD" polaroid from the desk. It develops as the site loads, gets a shake, then flies down and lands on its spot on the desk, where the 3D one takes over. Types and lint pass. I haven't seen the flight run yet: headless Chrome renders the 3D too slowly to capture it, so check http://localhost:3000 in your browser.

**What happens:**
1. **Loading:** the card copies the desk polaroid's layout (photo, frame, caption). The photo starts dark and blurred and fades in as the progress climbs. The caption reads `developing…` and the corner shows the real percent.
2. **Ready:** the caption changes to "it's me, JD" and the corner to "’26", same as the desk copy. The background fades away and the card shakes for 480ms.
3. **Flight:** the card moves to the polaroid's resting spot on the desk over 900ms, matching its position, size and rotation. When it arrives, the 3D polaroid appears in its place.
4. **Reduced motion:** no shake or flight. The 3D polaroid shows right away and the loader fades out as before.

**Changes:**
- [world.ts](src/components/hero/desk/world.ts): the desk polaroid stays hidden at rest, without its drop-in, until the card lands. A new function works out where it sits on screen.
- [DeskCanvas.tsx](src/components/hero/desk/DeskCanvas.tsx): hides `polaroid-me` from the start and passes its screen position up to the hero.
- [DeskHero.tsx](src/components/hero/DeskHero.tsx): the card replaces the progress bar and runs the develop, shake and flight steps. If the flight never reports finishing, the card lands anyway after 1.3s.
- [globals.css](src/app/globals.css): styles for the card and the develop, shake and flight effects.

The loader photo uses `me2.png` unoptimized, so it's the same file the desk loads and downloads only once. I haven't committed anything.

```bash
const SHAKE_MS = 480;
const FLY_MS = 2800;
const SWINGS = 2.5;

/*
 * A leaf's fall from the window centre to (x, y): it swings side to side,
 * leaning into each swing and lifting a little at either end, and the swings
 * die out as it settles at the polaroid's angle and size.
 */
function leafFall(x: number, y: number, angle: number, scale: number): Keyframe[] {
  const sway = Math.min(140, window.innerWidth * 0.1);
  const from = (-4 * Math.PI) / 180;
  return Array.from({ length: 61 }, (_, i) => {
    const t = i / 60;
    const p = t * t * (3 - 2 * t);
    const calm = (1 - t) ** 1.5;
    const swing = Math.sin(t * Math.PI * 2 * SWINGS);
    const lean = Math.cos(t * Math.PI * 2 * SWINGS);
    const tx = x * p + sway * swing * calm;
    const ty = y * p - 18 * Math.abs(swing) * calm;
    const rot = from + (angle - from) * p + 0.32 * lean * calm;
    return {
      transform: `perspective(900px) translate(${tx}px, ${ty}px) rotate(${rot}rad) rotateY(${28 * swing * calm}deg) rotateX(${12 * lean * calm}deg) scale(${1 + (scale - 1) * p})`,
    };
  });
}
''')
```

The print now drifts down like a leaf. Types and lint pass, but I haven't seen it run: headless Chrome renders the 3D too slowly to capture it. Check it at http://localhost:3000.

**How it moves now:**
- It swings side to side 2.5 times, up to 140px each way (10% of the window width on smaller screens).
- It leans into each swing and lifts a little at the ends, the way a falling leaf rises before dropping again.
- A small 3D tilt makes it flutter.
- The swings fade out near the bottom, so it settles exactly on the desk polaroid's spot, angle and size before the 3D polaroid takes over.
- The fall takes 2.8s instead of 0.9s, and the shadow tightens as it gets closer to the desk.

**Changes:**
- [DeskHero.tsx](src/components/hero/DeskHero.tsx): a new `leafFall()` works out the swaying path, and the card plays it as a script-driven animation instead of the old straight CSS move. The 3D polaroid appears when the fall finishes. If the fall never reports finishing, it lands anyway after 3.2s.
- [globals.css](src/app/globals.css): removed the old straight-line move. The shadow now changes over 2.8s.

**To tune it:** `FLY_MS` sets the speed and `SWINGS` the number of swings. `sway` sets how far it swings; it's inside `leafFall`. If you change `FLY_MS`, change the 2800ms shadow timing in the CSS too.

- The "The desk" title still fades out quickly when loading finishes.
- With reduced motion turned on, it's unchanged: a quick fade.

**Bigger photo for depth**
- The loading photo is now about 52% of the screen's shorter side, between 240px and 432px wide. Before, it was 34%, between 176px and 296px.
- The fall already shrank the photo to the desk polaroid's size, so it now shrinks more on the way down. That makes it read as moving away from you toward the desk.

Both changes are in [globals.css](src/app/globals.css). [DeskHero.tsx](src/components/hero/DeskHero.tsx) only gained one attribute the stylesheet needs (`data-print`).

**To tune:**
- **Fade length:** the `2400ms` background timing on `.desk-loader`.
- **Photo size:** the `--w` value on `.desk-print`.

```bash
D="C:/Users/Jeanne/AppData/Local/Temp/claude/c--Portfolio/51adf35a-3a24-4218-96a1-4fbfee76d61b/scratchpad"; rm -rf "$D/prof2"; cat > "$D/poll.mjs" <<'EOF'
const [,, port] = process.argv;
const list = await (await fetch(`http://127.0.0.1:${port}/json`)).json();
const page = list.find((t) => t.type === "page");
const ws = new WebSocket(page.webSocketDebuggerUrl);
let id = 0; const wait = new Map();
const send = (method, params = {}) => new Promise((r) => { const i = ++id; wait.set(i, r); ws.send(JSON.stringify({ id: i, method, params })); });
ws.onmessage = (e) => { const m = JSON.parse(e.data); if (m.id && wait.has(m.id)) { wait.get(m.id)(m.result); wait.delete(m.id); } };
await new Promise((r) => (ws.onopen = r));
await send("Page.enable");
await send("Page.addScriptToEvaluateOnNewDocument", { source: `
window.__log = []; const t0 = performance.now();
const tick = () => {
  const L = document.querySelector('.desk-loader'), P = document.querySelector('.desk-print');
  const c = document.querySelector('#intro > div');
  const ui = document.querySelector('.desk-ui');
  const s = (el, k) => el ? getComputedStyle(el)[k] : '-';
  window.__log.push([Math.round(performance.now()-t0), L ? L.dataset.print : 'gone', s(L,'backgroundColor'), s(L,'opacity'), s(c,'opacity'), P ? P.getAnimations().map(a=>a.playState+':'+Math.round(a.currentTime)).join(',') : '-', s(ui,'opacity'), document.documentElement.className].join(' | '));
  requestAnimationFrame(tick);
}; requestAnimationFrame(tick);` });
await send("Page.navigate", { url: "http://localhost:3000" });
await new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, 30000));
const r = await send("Runtime.evaluate", { expression: "JSON.stringify(window.__log)", returnByValue: true });
const log = JSON.parse(r.result.value);
let prev = "";
for (const line of log) { const k = line.split(" | ").slice(1).join("|"); if (k !== prev) console.log(line); prev = k; }
ws.close(); process.exit(0);
EOF
```

_**Agent (claude-opus-5-5 2026-10-29 16:10:14Z)**_

I found the cause of the pop and fixed it. In night mode, the loading screen's dark background never faded. A night-mode colour rule was more specific than my fade rule and overrode it. So the backdrop stayed fully dark through the whole drift, then disappeared at once when the photo landed. Day mode wasn't affected, which is why it only showed up in dark mode.

The fix is one selector in [globals.css](src/app/globals.css): `.desk-loader[data-print="flying"]` → `.desk-hero .desk-loader[data-print="flying"]`. That makes the fade rule outrank the night one.

I checked it in headless Chrome by logging the backdrop colour every frame in night mode. It now fades from solid to clear over the drift and is clear before the loader is removed (about 2.8s after the drift starts). The desk, wordmark and cards appear gradually underneath.

The one moment I couldn't check by eye is the hand-off from the HTML photo to the 3D polaroid. Headless Chrome renders the 3D too slowly to capture it. If anything still pops, it will be that swap, so look there at http://localhost:3000.

---

```text
const DARK_QUERY = "(prefers-color-scheme: dark)";

function subscribeDark(onChange: () => void) {
  const mq = window.matchMedia(DARK_QUERY);
  mq.addEventListener("change", onChange);
  return () => mq.removeEventListener("change", onChange);

/* Night follows the system theme until the visitor flips the lamp themselves. */
```

I fixed the pop and made day mode the default. Types and lint pass.

**The pop over "Dominique Paloma"**
The falling photo sits on a layer above the name. The 3D polaroid on the desk sits below it. So the instant the falling photo disappeared, the name appeared on top of the polaroid all at once.

Now, when the photo lands, the 3D polaroid appears underneath it first. The photo then fades out over 0.6s, so the name comes back over the polaroid gradually.

I tested it in headless Chrome by logging values every frame. The photo's opacity eases smoothly from 1 to 0 and the loader is removed only after that. The background stays clear the whole time. That test caught a bug I'd introduced along the way, where the brown background began to come back during the fade; I've fixed it. I still can't watch the final hand-off by eye in headless Chrome, so check it at http://localhost:3000.

**Day mode by default**
The desk now always opens in day mode, even if your system is set to dark. The lamp and moon button still switch to night. I removed the code that followed the system theme. That same test confirmed it loads in day mode even though headless Chrome is set to dark.

```text
export const chapters = [
  { id: "intro", href: "#intro", label: "Home" },
  { id: "features", href: "#features", label: "Features" },
  { id: "product", href: "#product", label: "Product" },
  { id: "contact", href: "#contact", label: "Contact" },
] as const;

/* not a page section: it flies the desk camera to the aquarium on the L return */
export const skillsLink = { href: "#skills", label: "Skills" } as const;

/* home: the link scrolls to the top, and the desk puts away whatever is open */
export const goHome = () => {
  window.dispatchEvent(new Event("desk:home"));
};

export const openSkills = (e: { preventDefault(): void }) => {
  e.preventDefault();
  window.dispatchEvent(new Event("desk:skills"));
};

/* whether the desk camera is at the aquarium, so the nav can mark Skills as current */
let tankOpen = false;
const tankListeners = new Set<() => void>();
export const tankView = {
  get: () => tankOpen,
  set(open: boolean) {
    if (open === tankOpen) return;
    tankOpen = open;
    tankListeners.forEach((l) => l());
  },
  subscribe(listener: () => void) {
    tankListeners.add(listener);
    return () => {
      tankListeners.delete(listener);
    };
  },
};

export type ChapterId = (typeof chapters)[number]["id"];

export const featurePanels = [
```

```text
"use client";

import { useEffect, useState, useSyncExternalStore } from "react";
import { tankView, type ChapterId } from "@/lib/chapters";

const sectionIds: ChapterId[] = ["intro", "features", "product", "contact"];

/* true while the desk camera is at the aquarium */
export function useTankOpen() {
  return useSyncExternalStore(tankView.subscribe, tankView.get, () => false);
}

export function useActiveChapter() {
  const [active, setActive] = useState<ChapterId>("intro");

  useEffect(() => {
    const sections = sectionIds
      .map((id) => document.getElementById(id))
      .filter(Boolean) as HTMLElement[];

    if (!sections.length) return;

    const observer = new IntersectionObserver(
      (entries) => {
        const visible = entries
          .filter((e) => e.isIntersecting)
          .sort((a, b) => b.intersectionRatio - a.intersectionRatio)[0];
        if (visible?.target.id) {
          setActive(visible.target.id as ChapterId);
        }
      },
      { rootMargin: "-40% 0px -40% 0px", threshold: [0, 0.2, 0.45, 0.7, 1] },
    );

    sections.forEach((el) => observer.observe(el));
    return () => observer.disconnect();
  }, []);

  return active;
}
```

```text
/* ── Project bookshelf ── */

export const SHELF = { x: 4.3, z: -3.0 };
const BOOK_W = 2.0;
const COVER = 0.05;
const THICK = [0.56, 0.48, 0.62, 0.5, 0.58];
const HEIGHT = [3.1, 2.9, 3.3, 3.0, 3.2];
const OPEN_SECONDS = 1.7;

const ease = (t: number) => (t < 0.5 ? 4 * t * t * t : 1 - Math.pow(-2 * t + 2, 3) / 2);
const phase = (p: number, a: number, b: number) => ease(THREE.MathUtils.clamp((p - a) / (b - a), 0, 1));

type ShelfProps = {
  projects: readonly BookProject[];
  open: number | null;
  /* hides the floating tag while something else has the reader's attention */
  quiet: boolean;
  reduced: boolean;
  onOpen: (index: number | null) => void;
  onHover: (index: number | null) => void;
    fwd: new THREE.Vector3(),
    right: new THREE.Vector3(),
    q: new THREE.Quaternion(),
  };
  private torch: THREE.SpotLight | null = null;
  private torchLevel = 0;
  private torchOnAt = -1;
  private clock = 0;
  private aim = new THREE.Vector3();
  private ray = new THREE.Raycaster();
  private plane = new THREE.Plane();
  hovered = -1;
  active: number | null = null;
  readonly shelfQ = new THREE.Quaternion().setFromAxisAngle(new THREE.Vector3(0, 1, 0), Math.PI / 2);
  readonly slots: THREE.Vector3[];

  constructor(count: number) {
    this.p = Array.from({ length: count }, () => 0);
    this.hover = Array.from({ length: count }, () => 0);
    let x = -2.25;
    this.slots = THICK.slice(0, count).map((t, i) => {
      const cx = x + t / 2;
      x += t + 0.04;
      return new THREE.Vector3(SHELF.x + cx, 0.2 + HEIGHT[i] / 2, SHELF.z + 1.0);
    });
  }

  attach(i: number, g: THREE.Group | null) {
    this.groups[i] = g;
  }

export function ProjectShelf({ projects, open, quiet, reduced, night, link, onOpen, onHover, onLoaded }: ShelfProps) {
  const camera = useThree((s) => s.camera) as THREE.PerspectiveCamera;
  const size = useThree((s) => s.size);
  const [tex, setTex] = useState<BookTextures | null>(null);
  const [anim] = useState(() => new ShelfAnim(projects.length));

  useEffect(() => {
    let alive = true;
    let built: BookTextures | null = null;
    buildBookTextures(projects).then((t) => {
      built = t;
      if (!alive) return;
      setTex(t);
      onLoaded?.();
    });
    return () => {
      alive = false;
      if (built) {
        built.paperEdge.dispose();
        built.books.forEach((b) => [b.spine, b.cover, b.left, b.right].forEach((x) => x.dispose()));
      }
    };
  }, [projects, onLoaded]);

  useEffect(() => {
    anim.setActive(open);
  }, [anim, open]);

  useFrame((state, delta) => anim.step(camera, size.width / size.height, delta, reduced, night, state.pointer, link));

  return (
    <group>
      {/* floating tag so the shelf reads as the way into the work */}
      {tex && open === null && !quiet && (
        <Html position={[SHELF.x, 0.3, SHELF.z + 1.7]} center zIndexRange={[15, 10]}>
          <button type="button" className="shelf-tag" onClick={() => onOpen(0)}>
            <span className="shelf-tag__dot" aria-hidden />
            Projects <span className="shelf-tag__count">{String(projects.length).padStart(2, "0")}</span>
          </button>
        </Html>
      )}

      {/* the shelf itself */}
      <group position={[SHELF.x, 0, SHELF.z]}>
        <mesh position={[0, 0.1, 0]} castShadow receiveShadow>
          <boxGeometry args={[4.9, 0.2, 2.2]} />
          <meshStandardMaterial color="#6b4428" roughness={0.6} />
        </mesh>
        {[-2.45, 2.45].map((x) => (
          <mesh key={x} position={[x, 1.9, 0]} castShadow receiveShadow>
            <boxGeometry args={[0.2, 3.8, 2.2]} />
            <meshStandardMaterial color="#6b4428" roughness={0.6} />
          </mesh>
        ))}
      </group>
```

```bash
/* where the desk is showing right now, so the nav can mark that link as current */
let current: DeskSpot | null = null;
const spotListeners = new Set<() => void>();
export const deskSpot = {
  get: () => current,
  set(spot: DeskSpot | null) {
    if (spot === current) return;
    current = spot;
    spotListeners.forEach((l) => l());
  },
  subscribe(listener: () => void) {
    spotListeners.add(listener);
    return () => {
      spotListeners.delete(listener);
    };
  },
```
```python
};"""),
```

```bash
const [,, port, url, out, waitMs] = process.argv;
const fs = await import("node:fs");
const list = await (await fetch(`http://127.0.0.1:${port}/json`)).json();
const ws = new WebSocket(list.find((t) => t.type === "page").webSocketDebuggerUrl);
let id = 0; const wait = new Map();
const send = (method, params = {}) => new Promise((r) => { const i = ++id; wait.set(i, r); ws.send(JSON.stringify({ id: i, method, params })); });
ws.onmessage = (e) => { const m = JSON.parse(e.data); if (m.id && wait.has(m.id)) { wait.get(m.id)(m.result); wait.delete(m.id); } };
await new Promise((r) => (ws.onopen = r));
await send("Emulation.setDeviceMetricsOverride", { width: 1440, height: 900, deviceScaleFactor: 1, mobile: false });
await send("Page.navigate", { url });
await new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, Number(waitMs)));
const s = await send("Page.captureScreenshot", { format: "jpeg", quality: 70 });
fs.writeFileSync(out, Buffer.from(s.data, "base64"));
ws.close(); process.exit(0);
EOF
```
